howIThink.title: How I engineer
howIThink.subtitle: End-to-end system thinking for critical financial infrastructure — every stage demands precision, foresight, and resilience.

steps.title: Architect for reliability
steps.body: Start with the assumption that the network and dependencies will fail — bake in idempotency, circuit breakers, and robust retry semantics from the first design doc.

steps.title: Contract before code
steps.body: Make data boundaries explicit: versioned API and event schemas lock in integration expectations before business logic flows.

steps.title: Make outcomes observable
steps.body: Trace user-impacting flows end to end: machine-readable logs, actionable metrics, and performance targets meaningful to real users, not just ops dashboards.

steps.title: Engineer for compliance and security
steps.body: Regulations and auditability are core requirements: model audit trails, access controls, and encryption as composable features, not bolt-ons.

howIThink.operatingBody: Financial infrastructure is not just code — it’s a web of durable guarantees: consistency when events collide, recoverability when things break, and predictable outcomes for every cent and every edge case.
bullets: Idempotency and strong transaction guarantees as table stakes, not tradeoffs
Provable auditability and traceability built into all critical flows
Security, controls, and compliance as pervasive building blocks, not late-stage concerns

items.title: Ecom 360 PME
items.problem: African retailers ran day-to-day operations on notebooks, spreadsheets, and improvised tills — cash errors, blind stock, forgotten customer credits, and end-of-day totals rebuilt by hand.
items.solution: All-in-one commerce platform: tactile POS, real-time inventory with low-stock alerts, Wave & Orange Money tied to each sale, multi-store management, customer credits, and accountant-ready PDF/Excel exports.
items.architecture: Angular SPA for POS and dashboards; Spring Boot multi-tenant REST API; async jobs for reports and bulk imports; store-scoped inventory and role-based staff access.
items.security: TLS in transit, encrypted sensitive data, automatic backups, tenant isolation per merchant, and role-based permissions for cashiers vs managers.
items.scale: Multi-store chains with consolidated reporting; mobile-first UX for counter, warehouse, and field; stock decremented on every sale without manual recounts.
constraints: Reliable counter operations, even with unstable network conditions.
Strict data separation by merchant and store.
Traceability for sales, customer credit, and mobile money payments.

decisions.title: Multi-tenant model
decisions.body: Centralize the platform while isolating operations, roles, and inventory per merchant.

decisions.title: Async jobs
decisions.body: Move exports, imports, and reports out of the checkout path to keep sales fast.

items.tradeoffs: The first version favored operational robustness over advanced analytics features.
items.bankingOutcome: Shows the ability to manage financial flows, local reconciliation, and multi-site operations with a minimum audit trail.
items.impact: 500+ active merchants across Senegal and West Africa; hours saved weekly on closing; local wallets recorded with every transaction instead of manual reconciliation.

items.title: Pan-African Payment SDK
items.problem: Products needed separate integrations for Orange Money, Wave, and Free Money — slow launches and inconsistent error handling across providers.
items.solution: Unified SDK exposing one API for initiate, confirm, and reconcile flows — provider-specific adapters behind a stable contract.
items.architecture: Adapter pattern with Spring Boot services, Redis idempotency keys, and Kafka events for async settlement notifications.
items.security: Signed requests, webhook HMAC validation, and per-tenant API keys with scoped permissions.
items.scale: Horizontally scaled stateless API; provider latency isolated via async queues without blocking client threads.
constraints: Heterogeneous provider APIs with inconsistent statuses and callbacks.
Retries must not create duplicate debits or duplicate notifications.
Shared observability across multiple payment corridors.

decisions.title: Unified contract
decisions.body: Expose a stable API while hiding Wave, Orange Money, and Free Money differences behind adapters.

decisions.title: Explicit idempotency
decisions.body: Treat every payment command with a stable business key to make retries safe.

items.tradeoffs: The adapter layer adds code, but it sharply reduces integration cost and provider-specific behavior drift.
items.bankingOutcome: Direct signal for banks and fintechs: unified Wave, Orange Money, and wallet integrations — patterns proven on ENG Technologie FinTech delivery and applicable to multi-provider banking corridors.
items.impact: ~60% faster integration time for new wallets; single observability surface across 3+ live providers.

items.title: Double-Entry Ledger System
items.problem: Financial products required auditable balances with strict consistency — spreadsheet-style tracking was not acceptable for compliance.
items.solution: High-consistency ledger with double-entry postings, immutable audit log, and transactional guarantees on every money movement.
items.architecture: PostgreSQL with serializable transactions for postings; append-only audit store; reconciliation jobs for provider drift.
items.security: Role-based access, immutable audit trail, and no destructive updates on posted entries.
items.scale: Partition-friendly schema and batch reconciliation for high-volume mobile-money corridors.
constraints: No balance should depend on destructive updates.
Every movement must be explainable to finance, audit, and compliance teams.
Reconciliation must detect provider drift before users do.

decisions.title: Append-only ledger
decisions.body: Record postings as immutable events to preserve the full financial history.

decisions.title: Serializable transactions
decisions.body: Favor financial consistency on critical paths, even with stricter concurrency handling.

items.tradeoffs: The model requires more domain discipline than a simple balances table, but avoids opaque corrections and untraceable drift.
items.bankingOutcome: Core signal for banking decision-makers: accounting correctness, auditability, reconciliation, and control of money movement — patterns applied on Synapse multi-entity banking delivery.
items.impact: Full auditability for regulators and finance teams; zero balance discrepancies in production reconciliation.

items.title: Unified API Gateway
items.problem: A multi-entity banking group and its partners needed one entry point to payment providers and internal services — without exposing fragile core systems. Patterns drawn from Synapse consultant delivery for Bank of Africa Group subsidiaries.
items.solution: Enterprise gateway centralizing auth, routing, rate limits, and provider orchestration behind versioned REST APIs — consultant-grade governance for regulated banking integrations.
items.architecture: Spring Cloud Gateway + domain microservices; Kafka for domain events; Jasper/reporting decoupled from transactional path.
items.security: JWT at edge, RBAC, input validation before core contact, full request audit logging.
items.scale: Stateless gateway tier; Kafka absorbs analytics peaks without blocking payments.
constraints: Protect core systems while opening partner APIs.
Version contracts without breaking existing integrations.
Trace every sensitive request for support, audit, and compliance.

decisions.title: Gateway as boundary
decisions.body: Centralize authentication, rate limits, validation, and routing before any internal system contact.

decisions.title: Decoupled events
decisions.body: Publish business events outside the transactional path for reporting and observability.

items.tradeoffs: The gateway becomes a critical governance point; it needs discipline around versioning, monitoring, and access policies.
items.bankingOutcome: Aligned with multi-subsidiary banking delivery: API governance, core protection, flow auditability, and faster partner onboarding across group entities.
items.impact: 3 partner integrations live; ~40% faster partner onboarding; 12+ months zero-downtime deploys.

items.title: School Management SaaS
items.problem: Private schools ran disconnected admin, billing, and academic tools — no single operational source of truth.
items.solution: Modern multi-tenant SaaS for admissions, billing, staff, and reporting — built for African school operations.
items.architecture: Angular + Spring Boot REST; async jobs for bulk operations; modular domains per school tenant.
items.security: Tenant isolation, encrypted sensitive records, role-based staff access.
items.scale: Async processing for reports and notifications; shared platform serving growing school networks.
constraints: Sensitive student, family, and finance data isolated by school.
Reporting must not block daily operations.

decisions.title: Modular domains
decisions.body: Separate admissions, billing, staff, and reporting so each area can evolve independently.

decisions.title: Shared platform
decisions.body: Serve multiple schools with one technical foundation and tenant-level rules.

items.tradeoffs: The shared SaaS model accelerates delivery, but requires strong tenant boundaries and clear per-school configuration.
items.bankingOutcome: Even outside banking, this case demonstrates multi-tenancy, sensitive data handling, billing, and structured operations.
items.impact: ~35% less admin handoff time; unified records across departments.
